title: Immunogenicity and Safety of AS03-adjuvanted H5N1 Influenza Vaccine in Children 6-35 Months of Age: Results From a Phase 2, Randomized, Observer-blind, Multicenter, Dose-ranging Study.
ehr_evidence: The study collected primary data through clinical trial visits, blood samples for serologic testing, cell-mediated immunity assessments, and adverse event reporting.
summary: Phase 2 randomized, multicenter, dose-ranging clinical trial evaluating the immunogenicity and safety of different formulations of an AS03-adjuvanted H5N1 influenza vaccine in children 6–35 months of age.
key_findings: All formulations elicited strong homologous immune responses with seroconversion rates of 100% and seroprotection rates of 100% at day 42.
The 1.9 µg HA/AS03B formulation ranked highest on the immunogenicity-fever index.
Antibody levels persisted >4 times above baseline at day 385 for all formulations.
Overall per-subject incidence of fever ranged from 28.6% (3.75 µg HA/AS03D) to 60.5% (1.9 µg HA/AS03B).
Grade 3 fever (≥39.0 °C) was reported in 18.4% of subjects in the 1.9 µg HA/AS03B group.
Serious adverse events were reported for 29 subjects (15.7%), none of which were fatal or related to vaccination.
captured_features: Geometric mean titers (GMT), seroprotection rate (SPR), seroconversion rate (SCR)
study_design: Phase 2, randomized, observer-blind, multicenter, dose-ranging clinical trial
population: Children 6–35 months of age (n=185) from Thailand and Taiwan
limitations: Absence of a placebo control to assess vaccine safety
Immunogenicity-fever index did not include other reactogenicity indicators
